title: Reasons 7-8: confession of the pagan crowd; nothing favors a multitude of gods
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): YE SEVENTH from ye sense plus confession belonging toward ye pagan crowd — they confess not many gods but under one great God many ministers. Tertullian: ye soul when it comes to senses names God alone — testimony belonging toward a soul naturally Christian. Lactantius: when they swear or give thanks they name God not many gods. YE EIGHTH: nothing can champion a multitude belonging toward gods. Hermes: one performs all these. Therefore God does all things. For this reason God unto unity is customarily compared.
pass_b_english: THE SEVENTH is from the sense and confession of the pagan crowd. Orosius: pagans confess that they do not follow many gods, but under one great God venerate many ministers. Tertullian (Apology 17): the soul, when it comes to its senses, names God alone — O testimony of a soul naturally Christian! Lactantius: when they swear or give thanks, they name not Jupiter or many gods but God.
THE EIGHTH: nothing can champion a multitude of gods. Hermes Trismegistus: one performs all these. Therefore God does all things. For this reason God is customarily compared to unity.
source_text: SEPTIMA est a sensu & confessione vulgi ethnicorum. Orosius: Pagani non se plures deos sequi, sed sub uno Deo magno plures ministros venerari fatentur. Tertullianus Apologet. 17: Anima, quum resipiscit, Deum nominat solum — O testimonium animae naturaliter Christianae! Lactantius: Quum jurant, quum gratias agunt, non Jovem aut deos multos, sed Deum nominant. OCTAVA: nihil est quod deorum multitudini patrocinari queat. Hermes Trismegistus: unus haec omnia praestat. Facit igitur omnia Deus. Hacpropter Deus unitati comparari consuevit.
